reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the rule's preferred position for NOSOLICIT is the absence of any non-solicit binding the Customer, so no-clause equals the preferred outcome rather than a 'missing' finding.
The redline is identical to the original paragraph and no comment was added, which is exactly what is expected for a compliant finding; nothing actionable is being proposed to the counterparty.

The cited paragraph (18.7 Entire Agreement) reasonably supports the rationale that no prior agreement, including the 2016 Confidentiality Agreement, survives to import a non-solicit or no-hire covenant.
The failed deterministic checks (duration ≤ 12 months, general-solicitation carve-out) are artifacts of there being no non-solicit language to test and do not undercut the compliance conclusion.
